question.problem: Consider the closed curve $C,$ which is the boundary of the region enclosed by $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and the $x$-axis, for $\pi \le x\le 2\pi .$ Express ${\int }_{C}xdx-(x-y)dy$ as a repeated integral.
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14227492/assets/264cb888010525848f647669653d34383535dd32e6ac264927105540c3b85f9f.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=x$ and $Q(x,y)=-(x-y).$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=0,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):\pi \le x\le 2\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x\le y\le 0\}
$$

Therefore, applying the Green's Theorem we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xdx-(x-y)dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1)\,\text{d}A \\  & =-{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}^{0}dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$
